1.mascotDialogue: All the splitting is just bookkeeping, beta — the real sorting work happens entirely in the merge step, comparing two already-sorted halves and interleaving them correctly. That's where the magic actually is.

2.mascotDialogue: Lines 9 and 10 are the merge's heart, beta — compare the fronts of both halves, take the smaller one, advance only that side. Lines 12 and 13 mop up whichever half still has leftovers once the other one runs out completely.

3.mascotDialogue: Notice this view does not show swaps at all, beta — merge sort doesn't swap elements in place! It writes the smaller of two fronts into a fresh position, every single comparison.

4.mascotDialogue: It is easy to think the merge is 'done' the moment the main comparison loop ends, beta — but one side almost always finishes before the other! And forgetting to drain the leftovers loses real data, quietly, without a single warning.
